headline: New York Rangers sign goalie James Reimer to 1-year contract
take:
The Athletic reports that the New York Rangers have signed goalie James Reimer to a one-year contract, noting he went 7-4-2 with an .886 save percentage for the Ottawa Senators last season. Daily Faceoff adds that Reimer appeared in one game for the Rangers' AHL affiliate before signing the new deal.

An .886 save percentage is below what teams usually want from a goalie, so the signing reads as depth rather than a fix. Our numbers suggest the Rangers don't have an obvious hole in net. So far this season, NYR sit at 7-5-1 with 15 points and a 51.9% share of expected goals (the share of shot quality they create compared with what they allow). Their goalies have saved 3.6 goals above expected, meaning they've stopped more shots than the quality of those chances would predict. That lifts results a bit, and it's a number to watch if it fades. Offense is the bigger gap: NYR are 1.7 goals below expected, so they're scoring less than their chances deserve. A goalie signing won't change that, but it covers the position if the current tandem falters or gets hurt.
